questions.question: How many interactive apps were included in the first EcoEvoApps release?
questions.rationale: The initial collection included 11 apps; a core subset was translated into five languages.
questions.evidence_quote: At the heart of ecoevoapps are 11 interactive apps (Table 1 )

questions.question: How does the package separate simulation from visualization in its R interface?

options.A: run_ functions take parameters, initial states, and time and return model output; plot_ functions take that output and return a ggplot2 object
options.B: plot_ functions run the differential equations, while run_ functions return ggplot2 objects
options.C: shiny_ functions return model data frames, while run_ functions launch hosted applications
options.D: run_ functions require precomputed figures, while plot_ functions execute simulations from raw experimental observations

questions.rationale: The package's interface pairs model-specific run functions that generate time-series data with plotting functions that visualize their output.
questions.evidence_quote: Simulations are conducted by functions with the prefix run_, which take as their input the parameter values and other relevant information for the particular model.

questions.question: What are the specific inputs and output of run_predprey_model()?

options.A: Parameter vector, initial predator/prey population vector, and time steps as inputs; a dataframe of population sizes over time as output
options.B: A ggplot object and two isocline coordinates as inputs; a fitted predator-prey model as output
options.C: Carrying capacity and predator attack rate only as inputs; a vector of equilibrium eigenvalues as output
options.D: A user-selected Shiny tab as input; a screenshot of the simulated trajectories as output

questions.rationale: The paper gives run_predprey_model as an example of the run_ interface, specifying parameter values, initial populations, and time and returning a time-series dataframe.
questions.evidence_quote: run_predprey_model() requires as inputs a vector defining the parameter values (params), a vector of the initial population sizes for the predator and prey species (init), and the time steps over which to run the model (time).

questions.question: Which extensions can users explore in the predator-prey dynamics app beyond the classic Lotka–Volterra model?

options.A: Logistic growth in prey, a type II predator functional response, or both together
options.B: Age-structured prey, disease transmission, or spatial diffusion
options.C: Adaptive evolution in predators, stochastic prey extinction, or both together
options.D: Competitive release, mutualism, and a three-species food web

questions.rationale: The app uses separate tabs for the classic model and extensions adding prey logistic growth and/or a type II functional response.
questions.evidence_quote: The app also includes three other tabs that incorporate logistic growth in the prey, type II functional response for the predator, or both.

questions.question: In the MacArthur–Rosenzweig predator-prey app, what qualitative change did increasing prey carrying capacity from K=200 to K=500 illustrate?

options.A: Damped oscillations occurred at K=200 when the predator isocline crossed right of the prey-isocline hump; unstable oscillations occurred at K=500 when it crossed left
options.B: Unstable oscillations occurred at K=200 to the right of the hump, while K=500 produced a stable equilibrium to the left
options.C: Both values produced stationary equilibria, but K=500 had higher predator abundance
options.D: K=200 caused prey extinction, while K=500 produced stable cycles because the predator isocline crossed the hump

questions.rationale: The example visualizes the paradox of enrichment: high carrying capacity shifts the isocline intersection to the left of the hump and destabilizes dynamics.
questions.evidence_quote: Panel A shows dampened oscillations arising at low prey carrying capacities (K = 200) when the predator (blue) isocline intersects the prey (red) isocline to the right of the "hump"

questions.question: What classroom evaluation supported the claim that EcoEvoApps helped students learn the models?

options.A: In a UCLA upper-division Ecology course, 40 of 51 students rated the apps 6 or 7 on a 1–7 scale for overall usefulness
options.B: In a UCLA introductory Biology course, 40 of 51 students improved exam scores by at least 40%
options.C: At Missouri, 51 of 51 students rated all model-specific topics as a 7
options.D: In a multi-institution survey, 40 of 51 students preferred lectures to interactive apps

questions.rationale: Students used Island Biogeography and Lotka–Volterra competition apps; 40/51 gave ratings of 6 or 7 for helping them understand the models as a whole.
questions.evidence_quote: An overwhelming majority of students (40/51) reported that the apps were moderately to very helpful for learning the models as whole (response of 6 or 7, Fig. 3A ).

questions.question: What was the pedagogical sequence in the UCLA classroom activity evaluated by the authors?

options.A: A roughly 15-minute video overview of the model/app followed by a worksheet-guided exploration
options.B: A 15-minute worksheet followed by a lecture explaining survey responses
options.C: A full-semester programming course followed by an unstructured group project
options.D: A live coding exam followed by a one-hour lecture on model history

questions.rationale: The activity paired a short explanatory video with a guided worksheet that led students through model exploration.
questions.evidence_quote: The learning activity included short (~15 minutes) video lectures that presented an overview of the model and the shiny app, followed by a worksheet that navigated students through a guided exploration of the model

questions.question: What limitation or scope imbalance did the authors identify for the initial EcoEvoApps collection?

options.A: The first release emphasized ecological models; future development would prioritize evolutionary biology and population genetics
options.B: The first release covered only evolutionary genetics, with ecological models planned later
options.C: The package was closed-source and could not be customized by EEB researchers
options.D: The apps required proprietary software and could not be run from R

questions.rationale: The collection's initial emphasis was ecological models; the authors explicitly identified evolutionary biology and population genetics as priorities for future additions.
questions.evidence_quote: Moving forward, we will prioritize incorporating mathematical models from evolutionary biology and population genetics into the package to complement the current ecological focus.

questions.question: What distinguishes EcoEvoApps from several other interactive EEB education resources, according to the authors?

options.A: It is entirely open-source and written in R, making it accessible and customizable by the EEB community
options.B: It uniquely includes only analytical solutions and no simulations
options.C: It is the only platform that requires a paid license for classroom use
options.D: It is restricted to hosted apps and does not expose model functions to users

questions.rationale: The authors emphasize the open-source R implementation as a distinguishing feature that supports community customization.
questions.evidence_quote: ecoevoapps is entirely open-source and written in R. As such, it is easily accessible and customizable by others in the EEB community

questions.question: What role do package vignettes serve beyond launching the apps?

options.A: They guide users in customizing/deploying app instances and in simulating model dynamics directly through R
options.B: They are required to upload survey data before an app can run
options.C: They contain only installation instructions and no model-specific material
options.D: They convert Shiny apps into non-interactive PDF figures

questions.rationale: The package includes a general deployment vignette and model-specific vignettes that teach direct simulation through the R console.
questions.evidence_quote: Finally, the package also includes model-specific vignettes with instructions for simulating the model dynamics directly through R
